Let me demonstrate by way of analogy. Have you ever played chess? I have, as a hobby, dabbled in it off and on throughout my life. Never getting super serious or anything but good enough to have gleaned a little insight. Assuming a level of play where you already understand how all the pieces move and you understand the basic types of attacks and defenses (forks, pins, etc) and maybe you already have a few favorite openings down... In my admittedly amateur understanding of the game it seems to me that one of the most easy ways to gain skill is to increase the number of moves ahead that one can plan. In normal, low stress play against people below my level I'll read maybe 7 moves ahead. 3 or 4 if I'm trying to handicap myself to make it more enjoyable for a complete neophyte. But if I get serious and I really want to win I'll get up as high as 15 moves or so.

Laymen often misunderstand what this entails and how this is done. Predicting that far into the future isn't just having a plan that includes 15 moves. It's planning so that no matter what move they make, unless you miss something, you have a plan for EVERY reasonable move they could make for the next 15 moves. A naive calculation would have a plan for every possible combination of moves for each of the next 15moves, so like given something like 10-15 pieces then you'd have maybe an average of 12^15 plans.

But then you realize you can trim this number of plans you have to make down significantly. First of all, if you assume a competent opponent then you can mark certain moves off the table immediately because they're either irrelevant or harm the opponent. If they make them you can just make minor adjustments to your plans but really it's like they give you free moves. Also, certain regions on the board can be grouped together because sets of moves will trigger predictable chains and must be resolved before moving on to other parts of the board otherwise your opponent will take unacceptable losses and if they do then you can just profit from it. But even then, you still have to think about a LARGE number of possible moves and have a plan for how to react no matter what they do.
This is what sets apart winners from losers for a very wide range of skill levels. Who can read the furthest ahead can react to upcoming problems early on to save themselves losses in the future or set opponents up for complex traps that bait them into bad situations.
